scene: one adult leans forward with both fists raised and the elbows bent, the front foot planted and the body driven towards a second adult who leans back with both arms lifted in front of the face and one foot stepping away. Their bodies are a step apart, not touching.
must: one adult lunging with both fists raised at another who steps back.
avoid: two adults facing each other with a bar each above the head (praten); two people shaking hands with a straight right arm (ontmoeten); two people with their hands on a ball between them (spelen); a weapon in a fist; a clenched fist held up alone (dreigen).
alt: Iemand komt voorover op een ander af met geheven vuisten; die stapt achteruit.

scene: SKIP: contributing means helping towards a shared result and shows only a hand putting something into a shared heap, which would be the picture of geven or verzamelen on this page.

one adult stands facing a shopkeeper, leaning forward over the counter with one fist pressed flat on the counter top and the other hand holding out an open bill in the shopkeeper's face; the shopkeeper leans back, hands raised. The receipt shows no digits.
must: an open bill pushed in a shopkeeper's face, a fist on the counter.
avoid: a note laid flat and calmly handed across the counter (betalen); a note offered flat on an open palm (bieden); a paper slipped into the slot of a ballot box (stemmen); a raised finger and a calm mouth (spreken).
alt: Iemand leunt over de toonbank met een vuist en houdt een rekening voor iemands gezicht.

scene: one adult knee-deep in the sea holds a stiff wide sheet of blue cloth by two corners and shakes it, so that the cloth lifts into a long curling roll across the frame with a sharp crest along the top. A row of small triangular flags runs along the beach behind.
must: a wide sheet of cloth arched into one curling roll, shaken by two hands.
avoid: a person wading waist-deep in surf (zwemmen); a cloth shaken like a flag (zwaaien); a boat with a big white sail (zeilen); flat still water with nothing in it.
alt: Een volwassene staat in zee en schudt een groot doek tot het in een lange krul opbolt.

scene: SKIP: the sense is to understand something, which is inner; any drawing of it is the thought bubble or the lightbulb, both A1 conventions this page may not use.

one adult stands in the middle of a room and turns the upper body round to the left, both feet still planted, one arm swinging across with the movement; behind them a second chair stands empty in the opposite corner. The head is turned over the shoulder, looking the other way.
must: feet planted while the body and head turn round the other way.
avoid: one adult walking behind another along a track (volgen); a hand held up flat at a car (stoppen); a door pushed against its frame (sluiten); a person walking in a full circle with both arms out (draaien).
alt: Iemand staat met vaste voeten en draait hoofd en bovenlichaam om naar achteren.

scene: one adult stands with a kite line in the open hand and lets it go: the line has left the fingers and the kite is drifting up and away to the right; the hand stays open in the air where the line was, and the face looks up after the kite.
must: a hollow open hand with the kite line already leaving it.
avoid: a balloon rising out of the same grasp; a cup falling from a hand (vallen); a hand stroking a cat; two hands gripping a handle to lift it (tillen).
alt: Iemand opent de hand en laat het touw van een vlieger schieten; de vlieger stijgt weg.

scene: SKIP: calling someone is the same mark as calling out, which is roepen, and the senses of summoning staff or calling a meeting are both a person speaking to a group or a telephone ringing.

one adult takes a baton from a second adult’s outstretched hand on a running track, the baton caught halfway between the two hands; the first body leans forward and the second arm is already falling back. A finish line lies far behind them and the track is otherwise empty.
must: a baton caught halfway between two hands on a running track.
avoid: a pen handed across a desk (geven); arms linked with both adults leaning forward together (samenwerken); a shop changing hands; an adult pulling a bag from another grip (pakken).
alt: Op een atletiekbaan neemt een loper het stokje over uit de hand van de vorige loper.

scene: One adult stands on a sandy path with both hands on the long handle of a spade, the blade driven in and a heap of sand half lifted in it, the shoulders turned and the eyes on the ground where a small hole shows; a wooden crate waits beside the hole, still empty.
must: a spade lifting a heap of sand beside a small hole.
avoid: an adult kneeling to press a spade downward into the ground (graven); a spoon lifting soup from a pot (koken); a barrow pushed with both hands along the path (duwen); a full crate carried in both arms (dragen).
alt: Een volwassene tilt met een schop een hoop zand uit een kuil omhoog, naast een lege kist.

scene: SKIP: the earlier sense is to look like, a comparison of two things that reads as lijken; the later sense, looking out over a view, is a person standing still and looking, which is the same picture as kijken.
